question: As per the 2011 Census, what percentage of the total population in India lives in rural areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**68.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2011 Census** indicates that** 68.84% of India's population** resided in** rural areas**, while only 31.16% lived in urban areas.
 
• This discrepancy is attributed to India's agrarian history, with many engaged in agricultural pursuits.
 
• Rapid urbanization and migration for employment have contributed to the urban population's growth, albeit at a slower pace than rural areas.
 
• Disparities in infrastructure and amenities between rural and urban regions further influence population distribution trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **2011 census of India,** also known as the 15th Indian census, occurred in two stages: house listing and population enumeration.
 
• The house listing phase commenced on April 1, 2010, focusing on gathering information about all buildings and also collecting data for the National Population Register (NPR), which aims to assign a unique 12-digit identification number to all Indian residents.
 
• The second phase, population enumeration, took place between February 9 and 28, 2011.
 
• This census marked the first instance of collecting biometric information since the census's inception in 1872.
